facts.text: On this date in 1492, Columbus's crew spotted land after 36 days at sea — but the island he called San Salvador is still disputed. Two Caribbean islands claim the title, and historians have never reached consensus.
On this date in 1968, NASA launched Apollo 7, the first crewed Apollo mission, from Cape Canaveral — just 21 months after a launchpad fire killed three astronauts in the same program.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than exist in the entire western half of the United States — roughly 170 million people within a radius smaller than many U.S. states.

Indonesia spans a wider longitude than the continental United States, yet nearly 60% of its 280 million people live on a single island — Java — making it the most densely populated large island on Earth.

The country with the world's highest median age is not Japan. It is Monaco, where the median resident is over 55 years old, partly because wealthy retirees relocate there specifically to avoid inheritance taxes.

On this day in 1987, the Dow had just begun its slide toward Black Monday. Within six trading days, it would lose 23% in a single session — still the largest one-day percentage crash in U.S. market history.

On October 11, 1962, the Vatican opened the Second Vatican Council. Within a decade, its modernization drive had made the Catholic Church one of the largest institutional landowners and art holders on Earth, a portfolio never formally valued.

The NYSE's 'buttonwood' origin story is partly myth. The 1792 agreement named after a tree was signed by 24 brokers — but trading had already been happening informally on Wall Street for years before anyone needed a treaty.
Saudi Aramco briefly held a $2 trillion market cap in 2019, making it worth more than the entire German stock market at the time.
The U.S. penny costs about 3.7 cents to produce. The mint has lost money on every penny since 2006, totaling over $1 billion in cumulative losses on a coin most people throw in drawers.
On this date in 1968, Apollo 7 became the first crewed Apollo mission. The astronauts also became the first humans to broadcast live TV from orbit — while battling head colds the entire flight.
On October 11, 1958, NASA launched Pioneer 1. It failed to reach the Moon but still traveled 113,800 km into space, accidentally teaching us the Van Allen belts were far larger than expected.
Your skeleton is not the rigid scaffold it appears. Bone is constantly dissolving and rebuilding itself — every decade, you have an almost entirely new skeleton.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
The immortal jellyfish, Turritopsis dohrnii, can reverse its own aging — reverting from adult back to polyp when stressed, then maturing again. It has no known limit to how many times it can do this.

On this date in 1968, Apollo 7 launched — the first crewed Apollo mission. It flew 50 years after WWI ended, yet only 5 years before the last Moon landing. The entire Moon era fits inside a single decade.
Oxford University was teaching students when the Aztec Empire was 400 years from existing. Oxford: est. ~1096. Aztecs founded Tenochtitlán: 1325.
On this date in 1776, Benedict Arnold's fleet was defeated at the Battle of Valcour Island — a loss that may have saved the Revolution by delaying the British long enough to end their 1776 campaign.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She died 30 BC. The pyramid was finished around 2560 BC. The Moon landing: 1969.
The fax machine was patented in 1843 — before the American Civil War, before the telephone, before the light bulb. Alexander Bain sent images over wire while Dickens was still writing novels.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Already feels ancient.
Hiraeth (Welsh): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to, or never had. Untranslatable in one word to English, which says something unflattering about English.
On this date in 1521, Pope Leo X granted Henry VIII the title 'Defender of the Faith' — the same faith Henry would soon rupture. The title still appears on British coins as 'F.D.'
Sillage (French, n.): the trail of scent left in the air after someone passes. Borrowed from the word for a ship's wake. Perfumers rate fragrances by it.

On this date in 1737, a cyclone struck the Ganges Delta and killed an estimated 300,000 people — one of history's deadliest storms, recorded by the British East India Company and largely forgotten by the world.
On Oct 11, 2011, Litecoin launched — the first major altcoin to swap Bitcoin's SHA-256 for Scrypt, explicitly to resist the ASIC mining rigs that were already centralizing Bitcoin's hashrate.
On Oct 11, 2016, Ethereum's Spurious Dragon hard fork erased 20 million empty accounts created by an attacker during the Shanghai DoS campaign, shrinking state size by roughly 80%.

Bitcoin's genesis block contains the headline 'Chancellor on brink of second bailout for banks' — not as metadata, but embedded directly in the coinbase transaction's scriptSig field, making it permanently unalterable.

The DAO hack of 2016 didn't steal ETH — it drained 3.6 million ETH into a child DAO governed by the same flawed code, giving the Ethereum community 27 days to respond before the attacker could move a single coin.
Satoshi's known addresses hold roughly 1.1 million BTC that has never moved — identifiable via the Patoshi pattern, a distinctive nonce-rolling signature in early blocks mined by a single entity.
On this date in 2012, Alex Krizhevsky submitted AlexNet to ImageNet. It won by a 10.8-point error margin so large that the computer vision field essentially restarted overnight.

Today in 2016, Google announced it had deployed TPUs internally for over a year before telling anyone — by then they had already processed more inference compute than the entire public cloud combined.

The transformer architecture has no recurrence and no convolution. When 'Attention Is All You Need' was submitted in 2017, several co-authors expected it to be a niche result for translation tasks only.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed roughly 50 GWh of electricity — comparable to the annual consumption of 4,500 average U.S. households, spent in a matter of months.

Reinforcement learning from human feedback was pioneered not for language models but for video game agents in the 1990s. It sat largely dormant for 25 years before becoming the dominant alignment technique in LLMs.
